[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Distributed Tracing, Logging, and Observability in System Design"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern distributed systems, such as microservices and serverless architectures, introduce significant complexity regarding debugging and monitoring. When a single user request traverses dozens of independent services, identifying the root cause of a latency spike or a failure requires robust observability practices."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Three Pillars of Observability"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Observability is built upon three foundational data types, often referred to as the three pillars:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Metrics: Numeric values measured over intervals of time, indicating the overall health and performance of the system."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Logs: Discrete, timestamped records of events that occurred within an application, providing rich contextual details about specific code executions."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Traces: Representations of the end-to-end journey of a single request as it propagates across multiple distributed services."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Distributed Tracing"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"In a monolithic application, call stacks are linear and local. In a distributed system, network boundaries separate components. Distributed tracing solves this by introducing the concepts of Traces and Spans."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Trace: The entire lifecycle of a request, composed of one or more spans."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Span: A single contiguous segment of execution time, containing metadata such as operation name, timestamps, tags, and logs."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Context Propagation"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To stitch together spans across network boundaries, services must propagate tracing context (such as trace ID and parent span ID) via request headers. Below is an example of injecting trace context into an HTTP request using OpenTelemetry concepts."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"import requests
from opentelemetry import trace

tracer = trace.get_tracer("my_service")

with tracer.start_as_current_span("outgoing_http_call") as span:
    headers = {}
    # Inject trace context into headers
    trace.get_current_tracer().inject(carrier=headers)
    response = requests.get("https://api.example.com/data", headers=headers)"},{"order":15,"type":"subheading","text":"Structured Logging and Correlation"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional plaintext logs make automated parsing and correlation nearly impossible at scale. Modern systems rely on structured logging (such as JSON) and inject active Trace IDs and Span IDs directly into log entries."},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"{
  "timestamp": "2023-10-25T14:32:10.123Z",
  "level": "ERROR",
  "service": "payment-service",
  "trace_id": "4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736",
  "span_id": "00f067aa0ba902b7",
  "message": "Payment gateway timeout"
}"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"By including the "trace_id" in your logs, an engineer can jump directly from a failed trace visualization in a tool like Jaeger or Zipkin to the exact log lines associated with that request in a log aggregator like Elasticsearch or Loki."},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for System Design"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Standardize on OpenTelemetry: Avoid vendor lock-in by using open standards for generating and collecting telemetry data."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Implement Sampling: Tracing 100% of requests in high-throughput systems is often cost-prohibitive. Use tail-based or head-based sampling to capture anomalies while dropping standard traffic."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Define Universal Semantic Conventions: Ensure all services use consistent naming conventions for attributes, spans, and metrics to streamline cross-team troubleshooting."}]
